reply_text:
Tracing which fragment of your codex-17 turn 象 read as a withdraw; then I'll send the three bells.Now the three bells. Checking which seats are idle.Fix 1 is running on codex-16. zai-5 refused fix 3: its usage limit is exhausted until 2026-10-06. I'm re-sending fix 3 to kimi-2.㊥ (line 2651 in codex-17, and the bells) The "withdraw inferred: unresolved (no target)" line in codex-17's buffer is a late notice about an earlier turn of yours, "You don't need to cancel, just do what I asked". It isn't about the turn it appears under. 象 read "You don't need to cancel" as you ending something codex-17 had done. It couldn't name what that was, so it recorded no target and nothing was undone. The notice arrived about four minutes after you typed that turn. By then you had sent your next turn and codex-17 had replied, so the notice landed under that exchange instead. Fix 1 is out to codex-16 and fix 3 to kimi-2. Fix 2 goes to codex-16 once fix 1 is back, because both edit the same function in `agent-chat.el`.

㊢ (timeline from 象's record `~/.emacs-graph/session-turn-analysis/turn-GYGJ2e.json`)
- 14:43:13: your turn 21, "You don't need to cancel, just do what I asked".
- 14:46:07: the analysis came back. "You don't need to cancel" was read as withdraw with `target null`. Its stated reason: the thing cancelled "is not named as an act id in the turn, so the target is left null rather than guessed". "just do what I asked" was read as continue.
- 14:47:09: the notice was shown in the buffer. The withdrawal post was answered `422 target-unresolved`. A negation interpretation was stored as `interpretation-negation:b53d095d…`, with resolution `target-unresolved`.

The thing being cancelled was codex-17's cancellation of the `patternrows1` job. That's a job, not an act with an `act:` id, so 象 had nothing to point at. Withdrawing it couldn't have restarted the job anyway.

㊩ (what's wrong with how it showed up) The reading itself looks right to me, and recording no target rather than guessing one is what's supposed to happen. The fault is in the display. The notice is inserted at the prompt whenever the analysis finishes, and it doesn't say which turn it belongs to. With a three-minute analysis, it can land under a later exchange, as it did here. Quoting the fragment in the line, e.g. `withdraw inferred on "You don't need to cancel": unresolved (no target)`, would be a small fix. I haven't sent that one out. Say if you want it.

㊢ (the bells)
- **Fix 1, codex-16:** a failed evidence record must not take the rest of the session down with it. The test plants a predecessor in `failed/` and checks that the next record still drains. Job `invoke-1790952744854-30384-e78c5dcb`, park `park-c62ef2ff-0ea7-4a91-82bb-eb3d81b33c58`; it's running.
- **Fix 3, kimi-2:** codex-repl should record its turns under the seat id rather than `codex`. kimi-2 first checks for consumers that select evidence by author `codex`, and stops if any would break. Job `invoke-1790952783868-30386-af3f9e02`, park `park-5045088d-6c41-461f-bb72-51fe48b5e4c4`; it's running. I first sent this to zai-5, which refused it with `429`: its weekly limit is exhausted until 2026-10-06 10:04.
- **Fix 2:** user turns should reply to the agent's last chat turn, not its turn-commits record. It's queued in fix 1's wake checklist, to go to codex-16 when fix 1 lands.

Both packets forbid reloading anything into your running Emacs and require batch ERT tests plus `check-parens`.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(what I checked)
- **The replay:** I posted the turns oldest first, 0.3 s apart. 154 came back `201`. The two I'd sent earlier came back `409 duplicate-id`, meaning they were already stored. Then I posted the five queued turns: your "Yes", codex-10's reply, and three later ones. All five came back `201`.
- **Your "Yes":** I fetched it back by id after posting it, and it's there.
- **What's left in the outbox:** four records are still in the queue. They're all stored now, so on its next pass the drain will get duplicates back and clear them.
- **What I didn't touch:** the `failed/` folder is unchanged. Those copies expire on their own after a day.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(why the agreement still fails) If an agent hasn't stored a formal offer, the route can make one from its reply, but only if the reply is marked 🈸 (`reply-offer!`, `futon3c/src/futon3c/transport/http.clj:10705`). Three things stop that here, and any one of them is enough on its own:
1. **The offer was marked ㊮ (collect), not 🈸.** The route only reads 🈸 paragraphs as offers.
2. **Your "Yes" replies to a commit record, not to codex-10's reply.** The turn your "Yes" answers (`in-reply-to`) is `emacs-c9b9…`, the record listing that turn's commits. That record is written after the reply, so it's the most recent evidence. The route needs an assistant chat turn there.
3. **The author doesn't match.** codex-repl stores its turns with the author `codex`, and the route compares that with `codex-10`. The fixed `"codex"` is passed at `futon3c/emacs/codex-repl.el:3371`.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (a record my check left behind) My agreement attempt wrote a refusal record, `agreement-refusal:6f3a6326…`. Recording refusals is what the route is meant to do, but this one came from my check, not from your keyboard.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(fixes) Each of these is a small change, so each would go out as its own bell:
1. Stop a failed turn from chaining: when the turn before is turned down for good, the next turn should not name it in `in-reply-to`. This is the chain defect from last turn.
2. User turns should reply to the agent's last chat turn, not to its commit record.
3. codex-repl should store its turns under the seat id (`codex-10`) rather than `codex`.
